articles.title: No more late salaries? UAE sees 151% jump in payroll processing as private-sector firms rush to meet new deadline - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UAE authorities have implemented a new wage payment rule requiring private sector employers to pay salaries on the first day of each month. This change, outlined in Ministerial Resolution No. 340 of 2026, has led to a significant increase in payroll processing activity across the private sector.  The UAE Central Bank and Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) jointly oversee the Wage Protection System (WPS), designed to ensure timely wage payments and strengthen compliance monitoring. The new rule has impacted small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) requiring them to adapt their cash flow planning and payroll schedules.  The implementation is part of broader UAE efforts to strengthen labour market governance, safeguard employee rights, and standardize wage payment practices across the private sector.

articles.title: India’s growth story remains strong, long-term outlook intact: Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jane Fraser, Chair of the Board and CEO of Citi, reaffirmed her confidence in India's long-term economic prospects, despite current global challenges.  She emphasized that while many economies face temporary headwinds, India's underlying growth potential remains robust. Fraser highlighted India's willingness to build for the future, its strategic importance to Citi, and its expanding role in the global artificial intelligence ecosystem. She also acknowledged that deal activity could slow down during the second half of 2026 due to geopolitical uncertainties and interest rate concerns but maintained a positive long-term outlook.

articles.title: Mutual funds avoid Rajesh Exports in last 10 years, LIC stake rose five times to 11% | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Exports, a gold and jewellery exporter, has been under scrutiny from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for allegedly inflating revenues over the past several years.  The company, listed since 1995, saw minimal domestic institutional investor interest, with mutual funds holding at zero percent in March 2023. LIC was the only significant domestic investor, increasing its stake from 1.99% to 11.22% over time. Foreign portfolio investors have held between 15.87% and 17.7% of the company's shares, with holdings declining in recent years.  Rajesh Exports has denied SEBI's findings, claiming that the discrepancy in revenue figures is due to a misunderstanding regarding the calculation of EBITDA for Valcambi, a Swiss gold refiner acquired by the company in 2015.

articles.title: Market wrap: Sensex closes flat, Nifty holds 23,400; Titan, Eternal lead gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex closed at 74,360, up nearly 14 points, while the Nifty 50 ended at 23,417, unchanged from the previous session.  Titan shares led gains on the Sensex, with Zomato-parent Eternal also seeing significant growth. The Indian Rupee closed at 95.7850 per US dollar, down slightly from Wednesday's close. Investors await the outcome of the Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting tomorrow.  The Nifty opened with a gap-down but recovered to close flat after finding support near its prior swing low for three consecutive sessions.

articles.title: Jet fuel price freeze: How the Rs 10,000-cr scheme affects airfares and airlines
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government has implemented a fixed price jet fuel scheme for participating airlines to stabilize airfares amid high international prices. The scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet, will see OMCs sell fuel at a fixed rate irrespective of market fluctuations, with losses being compensated from a stabilization fund.  This temporary arrangement is expected to ease financial pressure on both Indian airlines and OMCs for up to three years.

articles.title: Quantum Computing Is Having Its Public Market Moment | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Quantinuum, a quantum computer maker, is set to debut on the New York Stock Exchange this week despite facing financial challenges and skepticism about its technology's commercial viability. The company has seen significant revenue decline and lost nearly $200 million last year.  Despite these concerns, investor demand for Quantinuum shares has surged, leading to an increase in the price and number of shares being issued. This surge in interest is fueled by the growing popularity of quantum computing and a recent government investment in the field.

articles.title: Hero MotoCorp shares rise 3% as firm unveils India's first 100cc flex-fuel motorcycles. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hero MotoCorp, India's largest two-wheeler manufacturer, launched flex-fuel versions of its flagship Splendor+ and HF Deluxe motorcycles. The new models are compatible with ethanol-blended fuels ranging from E20 to E85 and aim to reduce carbon footprint while aligning with India's goal of lowering economic carbon intensity by 45% by 2030.  The launch was unveiled in New Delhi ahead of World Environment Day, attended by Union Ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri, as well as Harshavardhan Chitale, CEO of Hero MotoCorp. The motorcycles will be available in select regions of Maharashtra and Delhi from July 2026.

articles.title: 'No Revenue Inflation': Rajesh Exports Rejects Rs 15 Lakh Crore Scam Charge
articles.rephrased_article: Rajesh Exports, a gold refining and jewelry giant, has denied allegations of Rs 15.15 lakh crore revenue inflation by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The company claims a communication gap caused the misunderstanding with SEBI and insists its revenues are accurate.  The Bengaluru-based company is submitting additional documents to the regulator and believes the investigation will clear up the concerns raised.  SEBI's interim order, which barred Rajesh Mehta from buying or selling securities of the company, has triggered a selloff in Rajesh Exports shares.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of a massive financial scam against a major company raise serious concerns.

articles.title: Reliance traders said to game plan in case RBI raises rates - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance, one of India's largest conglomerates, is considering shifting its cash holdings from liquid mutual funds to short-dated money market instruments. This strategy aims to capitalize on the widening yield spread between money-market papers and benchmark rates, which is expected to narrow in the coming months. The conglomerate also discussed reducing allocations to longer-dated bonds due to their sensitivity to interest rate changes. Reliance's traders anticipate a stronger rupee if a Middle East peace deal occurs and the RBI takes measures to attract capital inflows.

articles.title: US economy remains strong, India must accelerate reforms and AI adoption: Ajay Srivastava - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Srivastava, an economic expert, believes the U.S. economy is strong and resilient despite geopolitical tensions. He argues that India should focus on its own economic challenges rather than comparing itself to other nations.  He sees significant opportunity for Indian businesses in AI adoption, particularly within the banking sector.  Srivastava also emphasizes the importance of global diversification for long-term wealth creation, urging Indian investors to expand their portfolios beyond domestic assets.

articles.title: Audio book platform Kuku files confidential papers for up to Rs 3,500-cr IPO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kuku Technologies, a company specializing in audio and video content, is planning to raise between Rs 2,500-Rs 3,500 crore through an IPO. The offering will comprise a mix of fresh issue shares and an offer-for-sale (OFS) by existing investors.  The proceeds will be used for technology and AI infrastructure development, content creation, and expansion into new markets. Kuku Technologies, founded in 2018 by IIT alumni Lal Chand Bisu, Vinod Kumar, and Vikas Goyal, has seen significant revenue growth, reaching over Rs 1,400 crore in FY26. The company's platforms, including Kuku FM, Kuku TV, and Guru, have garnered over 10 million active paying subscribers and more than 400 million cumulative downloads across seven to eight Indian languages.

articles.title: ICICI Bank shares fall 10% in 6 months. Here’s why Motilal Oswal sees 41% upside potential - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Bank shares gained over 1% on Thursday, trading at Rs 1,258.40 apiece, despite a recent decline in value. Motilal Oswal, a domestic brokerage firm, maintains its bullish call on the bank's stock, citing strong growth momentum and profitability benchmarks. The brokerage expects ICICI Bank to deliver a 16% loan CAGR over FY26-FY28, driven by robust business banking and private lending (PL) growth, while corporate segment activity is expected to improve. Motilal Oswal also highlighted the bank's strong liability franchise, healthy asset quality, and cost leadership despite investments in technology and talent.  The brokerage expects a gradual rerating of ICICI Bank shares, maintaining its "Buy" call with a target price of Rs 1,750 apiece.

articles.title: Jefferies initiates coverage on Poonawalla Fincorp with Buy rating. Why are analysts bullish? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies analysts are optimistic about Poonawalla Fincorp's future growth, citing its revamped leadership team, expanded product portfolio, and improved credit quality. The brokerage projects a 33% annualized asset under management (AUM) growth rate for the company over FY26-29, driven by investments in distribution, technology, and AI.  They anticipate significant improvements in profitability, with RoA/RoE expected to reach 16% by FY29 from 6% currently. The brokerage also highlights the company's strong capital position and AAA credit rating as positive factors. Despite trading at a premium valuation, Jefferies believes Poonawalla Fincorp's growth trajectory justifies its current price.

articles.title: UBS downgrades BHEL shares to Neutral from Buy. Check target, key reasons - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: UBS downgraded its rating on BHEL stock, citing increased competition in the industry. Despite this downgrade, UBS maintains a positive long-term outlook for the company, attributing it to strong order book visibility and steady revenue growth from thermal power and industrial segments. The brokerage expects BHEL's earnings to exceed market expectations, raising its FY27 and FY28 forecasts by 1-3%.  BHEL reported significant financial performance in FY26, with a 200% surge in net profit and a 19% increase in revenue.

articles.title: Visible Promo Codes and Coupons for June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Visible, a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO), offers two unlimited plans for as low as $25 per month, using Verizon's 5G and 4G LTE networks. The company provides an eSIM travel pass for international travelers, offering unlimited data and text in the US, Canada, and Mexico. Visible also offers promo codes for discounts on various plans, including a special offer for new members with a Back Market phone.  For those looking to save money, Visible offers a plan starting at $20 per month for 12 months when using the promo code FRESHSTART.

articles.title: H&R Block Coupon: 25% Off DIY + Tax Pro Assist | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: H&R Block offers various tax preparation services to help individuals navigate the complex process. The company provides both in-person and online options, including a free edition for simple returns and paid tiers with additional features like Pro reviews and investment support. H&R Block also offers discounts and coupons through its website to make filing taxes more affordable.  Taxpayers can choose from different services based on their individual needs and financial situation.

articles.title: 'Inflated Bills, Gold Mine': Rajesh Exports And A Rs 15 Lakh Crore Question
articles.rephrased_article: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) barred Rajesh Exports and its promoter-chairman, Rajesh Mehta, from accessing the securities market due to allegations of massive revenue misrepresentation spanning five financial years. The regulator alleges that nearly all of Rajesh Exports' reported revenues came from overseas subsidiaries, with a discrepancy of Rs 15.15 lakh crore in reported revenues compared to verified subsidiary records. SEBI also questioned investments in gold mining assets in Africa and transactions involving Affluence Shares Pvt. Ltd., raising concerns about the company's financial health and governance.  The investigation is ongoing, and Rajesh Exports denies all allegations, while investors have reacted with severe market punishment for the company.

articles.title: US plans additional 12.5% tariff; India says talks on Section 301 probes ongoing - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) proposed new tariffs on most Indian goods, citing concerns about forced labor and excess industrial capacity. India is engaged in discussions with the US regarding these issues under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974. The USTR also launched separate investigations into excess industrial capacity in 60 countries, including India and China.  The proposed tariffs would affect a wide range of products, but certain sectors like textiles and pharmaceuticals are excluded. India is expected to challenge these measures, arguing that the investigation exceeds its scope and that the US should address forced labor concerns more specifically.

articles.title: Aditya Shah favors domestic growth themes, stays bullish on IT and infrastructure sector - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shah, a prominent investor, advises focusing on EPC contractors, road contractors, and established players like L&T in the infrastructure sector due to strong order books. He remains constructive on the IT sector despite AI concerns, highlighting companies like TCS and HCL Tech.  He suggests evaluating opportunities on a company-by-company basis rather than broad sector bets. While optimistic about India's cell manufacturing potential, he cautions about Ola Electric's customer support issues and advises waiting for further evidence of improvement before investing. He prefers domestic growth themes like chemicals, infrastructure, banks, and financials over metal stocks due to easing valuations. Despite challenges in the airline industry, Shah remains positive on IndiGo's dominant market position and expects near-term earnings pressure but continued market share gains.  He believes any resulting market correction presents an opportunity for long-term investors.

articles.title: Exclusive | Is the India story over for FIIs? BofA says investors don't want to miss what's next - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors are cautiously optimistic about India's economic prospects, acknowledging the cyclical nature of the market. While Q4 earnings showed a marginal beat, overall growth remains muted due to commodity-driven earnings and concerns over inflation. FIIs have been pulling out capital, citing alternatives in other markets and India's weak performance.  The Indian government needs to address energy security, fiscal consolidation, and regulatory reforms to attract foreign investment and boost investor confidence.

articles.title: IT stocks crash! Planning to buy the dip? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty IT index plunged nearly 6% on Wednesday, driven by profit-taking after a recent surge.  Analysts attributed the decline to AI fears and concerns about long-term growth in traditional IT services companies. While some analysts believe the market correction is temporary, others caution that valuations remain high despite slowing growth. Harshal Dasani from INVasset PMS suggests that the weakness in IT stocks is not solely due to AI disruption but also reflects a lack of earnings visibility and potential for AI-led revenue acceleration.

articles.title: TurboTax Full Service Coupons This June | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: TurboTax offers various self-filing options, including free versions for qualifying taxpayers and paid services with expert assistance.  The company provides discounts on federal and state tax filings, as well as referral programs that offer gift cards to users who refer friends. Intuit, the parent company of TurboTax, also offers a Tax Refund Calculator and a Tax Bracket Calculator to help users estimate their taxes.

articles.title: Walmart Promo Codes: Up to 65% Off for June 2026 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Walmart offers a wide range of products and services, including flash deals, online shopping with pickup and delivery options, and its own membership program called Walmart+.  The program provides free grocery delivery, free shipping with no order minimum, savings on fuel, and early access to promotions. Walmart+ also includes a 30-day free trial and is available for monthly or annual payments. The retailer also offers fast delivery options in as little as an hour, including delivery of essential medications like insulin.  Additionally, Walmart provides discounts on diabetes essentials, such as glucose monitors and insulin coolers, to help manage the cost of medical care.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX IPO, priced at $135 per share, could make him world’s 1st trillionaire | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket and artificial intelligence company, has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $135 per share, aiming to raise $75 billion. The offering, scheduled to begin trading next Friday, would make it the largest public offering in history, surpassing the $29.4 billion raised by Saudi Aramco in 2019.  The IPO could also cement Elon Musk's status as the world’s first trillionaire.

articles.title: Sensex Today, Stock Market LIVE Updates | Nifty | Share Market: Sensex, Nifty Likely To Open In Red Amid Negative Global Cues
articles.rephrased_article: Indian equity benchmarks continued their downward trend on Thursday, with the Sensex and Nifty50 opening lower. The rupee opened unchanged at 95.71 against the US dollar.  Crypto markets experienced a selloff driven by factors like ETF outflows, geopolitical uncertainty, and technical breakdowns.  The Indian government announced it will eliminate capital gains tax on foreign portfolio investments in government securities to attract more foreign capital. Global markets are cautious due to rising crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and the upcoming RBI policy announcement.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX eyes $1.77tn valuation ahead of blockbuster IPO | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket company, is aiming for a valuation of nearly $1.77 trillion in its blockbuster initial public offering (IPO), seeking to raise approximately $75 billion by selling 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece.  This would make SpaceX the world’s seventh-largest company by market capitalization and surpass Saudi Aramco's 2019 debut. Despite a lack of profitability, investors are betting on SpaceX's future growth in areas like rockets, satellite internet, and artificial intelligence. The IPO is expected to trade on the Nasdaq stock exchange from June 12th.

articles.title: Modi Government On Capital Gains Tax: India's Big Move To Attract Foreign Investment Amid Iran War: Sources
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Cabinet, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved an ordinance amending the Income Tax Act to eliminate capital gains tax on investments made by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in Indian government securities. This move aims to attract more foreign capital inflows and mitigate the adverse effects of the Iran war on the economy. The decision comes after calls for tax cuts to prevent further outflows from the Indian stock markets, which have seen significant withdrawals from FPIs this year.  The ordinance will be implemented after Presidential approval.

articles.title: Indonesia’s rupiah falls to record low against US dollar | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia’s rupiah has reached its record low against the US dollar, breaching 18,000, due to surging energy costs caused by the Iran-US war.  The country is a net oil importer and faces pressure from high crude prices, leading to a narrowed trade surplus and increased demand for dollars. Bank Indonesia, the central bank of Indonesia, has attempted to stabilize the currency through rate hikes and foreign exchange interventions but has been unsuccessful.

articles.title: Kerala faces burden of ₹5.07-lakh crore liabilities; fiscal structure under ‘serious’ strain, says White Paper tabled by CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan tabled a white paper in the State Assembly on Thursday, June 4, 2026, highlighting Kerala's fiscal strain. The document states that the state faces a large burden of outstanding liabilities and high interest payments, while its capital expenditure is among the lowest in India despite a high fiscal deficit.  The white paper also points to "parallel governance structures" like the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) as contributing to the fiscal stress.

articles.title: Rupee falls amidst gulf tensions and rising oil prices - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian rupee traded between 95.80 and 95.44 on Tuesday, experiencing appreciation due to RBI intervention and positive news regarding government efforts to attract foreign capital. The currency has weakened by 0.9% in FY27 and nearly 11% in FY26.

articles.title: Chintan Research Foundation Organises Policy Dialogue On Small Modular Reactors
articles.rephrased_article: Chintan Research Foundation (CRF) and Finovista, in partnership with Manthan, an initiative of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, hosted a Policy Dialogue on "Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) for Defence Manufacturing & Data Centre Operation" in New Delhi. The dialogue brought together policymakers, industry leaders, and experts to discuss the role of SMRs in supporting India's energy transition and strengthening critical sectors like defence manufacturing and data centres. Dr Debajit Palit, Centre Head, Centre for Climate Change and Energy Transition at Chintan Research Foundation, highlighted that SMRs can provide a low-carbon clean energy source for India while also meeting the power needs of defense manufacturing and data centers.

articles.title: IRCTC reinforces its AI monitoring system to ensure hygiene and quality of food in trains | Business News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: IRCTC, the Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation, has expanded its AI-based food hygiene monitoring system to over 800 kitchens. The system uses 2,394 cameras to detect nine factors contributing to unhygienic food practices, including hairnet compliance and rodent presence.  The system generates around 350 alerts daily, with the North Zone experiencing the highest number of violations. While the system has been effective in reducing complaints, it occasionally flags false positives due to its programming. The Railway Ministry imposed fines on IRCTC for serving poor-quality food and the company supplying food in a Vande Bharat train.

articles.title: Brokers prepare rollout of algo trading tools for retail investors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brokerage firms are expanding their services by offering algorithmic trading (algo) strategies to retail clients. The move, driven by regulatory clarity and the need for revenue growth, allows brokers to charge fees for access to these pre-set trading algorithms. HDFC Securities, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, and other large traditional brokers already offer algo services.  Raise Securities, which owns the Dhan trading platform, recently acquired an algo provider startup. Other firms like Angel One, Upstox, SBI Securities, Kotak Securities, IIFL Capital Services, and 5paisa are also preparing to launch these services. The adoption of algo strategies is expected to increase as they offer convenience and automation for retail traders, particularly in derivatives trading.

articles.title: Brokers prepare rollout of algo trading tools for retail investors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brokerage firms are expanding their services by offering algorithmic trading (algo) strategies to retail clients.  The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has implemented a framework for safer participation in algo trading since April 2026, requiring brokers to obtain exchange approval, tag orders for audit trails, monitor APIs, and handle investor grievances. This regulatory clarity has spurred many traditional brokers like HDFC Securities and Motilal Oswal Financial Services to offer algos, while others are in the process of launching these services.  Angel One, Upstox, SBI Securities, Kotak Securities, IIFL Capital Services, and 5paisa are also preparing to provide algo strategies to clients.

articles.title: Electric vehicles: Costly fuel pushes more Indians to buy EVs yet obstacles remain
articles.rephrased_article: India's automobile market is experiencing a surge in electric vehicle adoption, driven by rising fuel prices and upcoming regulations. The market for electric cars expanded 25% in the year ending March 2026, with EVs crossing the 5% threshold in passenger vehicles.  Analysts predict that India will see a significant increase in EV penetration over the next decade, particularly in high-usage categories like three-wheelers and two-wheelers. However, challenges remain, including limited charging infrastructure, reliance on global supply chains for battery components, and uncertainty surrounding regulatory clarity.

articles.title: Why Canada has generic Ozempic, and the US doesn't
articles.rephrased_article: Canada became the first G7 country to approve a generic semaglutide injection, intended for type 2 diabetes patients but can be prescribed off-label for weight loss. The discounted medications are expected to be available in pharmacies across Canada as of June, at less than a third of the cost of brand-name drugs. This development is expected to make GLP-1 drugs more accessible to Canadians and may also prompt similar efforts in the United States, where generic versions are not expected until 2032 due to patent laws.  The arrival of generics has prompted Novo Nordisk to lower prices of its brand-name drugs, but the company maintains that the situation in the US is different and it will continue to fight for its patent rights.

articles.title: CREDAI discusses with CM Vijay issues concerning real estate sector in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay
articles.rephrased_article: CREDAI, the Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India, met with Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss issues affecting the state's real estate sector. The delegation highlighted concerns regarding delays in approvals and requested a streamlined single-window system for faster project execution. They also raised concerns about the Ramsar designation on Pallikaranai Marsh, impacting landowners and hindering access to financial services. CREDAI proposed scrapping the designation or establishing a committee to complete the notification process within 30 days.  They further advocated for expanding the scope of self-certification and automatic building approval systems under the single-window mechanism.

articles.title: An app to help eateries sell surplus food - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode entrepreneurs Muhammed Nihal V. and Hiba Nourin K.P. are launching an app called Kyka, which connects eateries with customers to sell surplus food at discounted prices. The app, available on Google Play and the App Store from June 10th, operates on a "triple impact model" that reduces food waste, generates revenue for restaurants, and provides affordable meals for consumers.  The Kozhikode Corporation is supporting the initiative, which will initially operate in Kozhikode before expanding to other locations in Kerala and potentially beyond.

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi to launch, lay stone for infra initiatives worth Rs 18K crore in Surat tomorrow | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone for several development projects in Surat, Gujarat, worth over Rs 18,000 crore. These initiatives include four National Highway projects, two packages of the Vadodara–Mumbai Expressway, eight GIDC projects, and upgrades to the Hazira Port–Surat section of National Highway 53. The projects aim to strengthen connectivity, boost economic development, and improve freight movement along the Delhi–Mumbai expressway.

articles.title: What is the St Petersburg forum, Putin’s economic outreach to the world? | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Ukrainian drone strike near St. Petersburg disrupted operations at the city's airport hours before the start of the St Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF). The annual event, often called "Russia's Davos," is expected to attract 20,000 guests from over 130 countries and features discussions on topics such as energy markets, artificial intelligence, and information warfare.  President Vladimir Putin, who typically attends the forum, will deliver a keynote address outlining Russia's economic priorities and foreign policy ambitions. Rodney Mims Cook Jr., chairman of the US Commission of Fine Arts, is among the notable attendees representing the United States. The forum also features representatives from countries like Uzbekistan, Tanzania, China, Saudi Arabia, and Belarus.  The event serves as a platform for Moscow to showcase its economic resilience amidst Western sanctions and promote international partnerships beyond the West.

articles.title: US stocks today: Dow Jones drops over 500 points as Middle East tensions escalate - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all closed in negative territory on Tuesday, dragged lower by financials and tech.  While the artificial intelligence sector showed resilience, concerns over geopolitical tensions and inflation persisted. The Middle East hostilities intensified, oil prices rose, and the Federal Reserve's December meeting rate hike probability increased. Despite positive economic data, corporate spending plans appeared soft amid rising energy costs.

articles.title: SpaceX Aims To Raise Record $75 Billion In Stock Market Debut: Report
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket and satellite company led by Elon Musk, plans to raise approximately $75 billion through a record-breaking initial public offering (IPO). The company will sell 555,555,555 shares at an initial price of $135 each. This move would surpass the previous record held by Saudi Aramco, which raised $25.6 billion in 2019.

articles.title: Amazon Employees Show Up to City Council Meeting to Demand Limits on Data Centers | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Two Amazon employees, Liesl Wigand and Patrick Schloesser, publicly urged Seattle officials to regulate new data center construction, citing environmental, economic, and safety concerns. They advocated for increased renewable energy use, power storage, and worker-led safety committees.  The comments mark a significant escalation in the nationwide protest against rapid data center development, with workers from various tech companies expressing similar concerns. Amazon did not immediately comment on the employees' statements. Seattle is considering a one-year pause on issuing permits for new data centers to establish regulations.

articles.title: Thali costs climb in May: Crisil report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Crisil predicts elevated tomato, potato, and onion prices in the coming months due to lower production and supply constraints. Tomato prices are expected to remain high through June-August as summer sowing is impacted by heat concerns in key growing states.  Potato prices will also increase as the rabi harvest season concludes. On the other hand, Crisil expects pulses prices to remain subdued due to ample domestic availability.

articles.title: The Great Chinese Factory Glut Is Starting To Choke The World
articles.rephrased_article: China's total non-financial sector debt has reached 313% of GDP and is projected to reach 323% by 2026. This rising debt, coupled with declining efficiency of investment, suggests a weakening growth model that relies heavily on capital formation rather than household demand.  The country's property slowdown, falling land sales, and demographic decline are exacerbating the situation. IMF estimates show China is operating with a negative output gap and core inflation remains low. This economic imbalance has led to an oversupply of goods in export markets, particularly electric vehicles and solar panels, which are flooding global markets despite tariffs.  The "New Three" sectors - electric vehicles, batteries, and solar manufacturing - reflect this struggle for domestic demand.

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 10,000-Crore Fund Amid Rising Jet Fuel Prices
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government approved a Rs 10,000 crore aviation fuel price stabilization fund to mitigate the impact of rising global prices.  Information Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that the fund will help stabilize aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices for airlines and prevent disruptions in operations. The fund is expected to protect 77 lakh jobs dependent on the aviation ecosystem and safeguard public investment in airport infrastructure. It will be in effect for 36 months, with annual reviews or until the advance amount is fully recovered/settled.

articles.title: We expect interest rates to be left the way they are: Ficci chief Anant Goenka - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RPG Group's vice-chairman, Goenka, expressed optimism about India's economic future despite concerns over foreign capital outflows. He advocated for continued ease of doing business and a focus on key sectors like data centers and semiconductors, while acknowledging the impact of the West Asia conflict on GDP growth. Goenka also emphasized the importance of leveraging free trade agreements (FTAs) to boost manufacturing and highlighted that recent market corrections have led to FPIs returning. He believes India's markets are now more fairly valued after a period of overvaluation.

articles.title: We expect interest rates to be left the way they are: Ficci chief Anant Goenka - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RPG Group vice-chairman, Goenka, expressed optimism about India's economic outlook despite concerns over foreign capital outflows and potential GDP impact from the West Asia conflict. He advocated for maintaining current interest rates and minimizing rupee intervention while emphasizing the need to leverage free trade agreements (FTAs) and focus on key sectors like data centers and semiconductors. Goenka also noted that recent corrections in Indian markets may lead to a return of foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).

articles.title: Norms issued to estimate District Domestic Product - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released guidelines recommending the use of various data sources to estimate economic activity in different sectors. These include GST collections for trade, hotels, and restaurants; Annual Survey of Industries data for organized manufacturing; Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises for informal sector activities; and RBI banking statistics for financial services. The guidelines also reflect the recent revision of the national gross domestic product (GDP) base year to 2022-23. These recommendations aim to support evidence-based policy formulation, regional development analysis, and informed decision-making at the district level.

articles.title: RBI likely to hold rates as West Asia crisis impact on growth remains unclear: Bank of Baroda Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is expected to maintain interest rates on Friday, June 5th, as the impact of the ongoing West Asia crisis on economic growth remains unclear. The central bank will likely continue its data-dependent approach, balancing growth concerns with inflation risks and global uncertainties. articles.title: ADB, StanChart ink partnership to support Indian firms across supply chains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Standard Chartered Bank have signed agreements to strengthen supply chain finance in India. articles.title: Jefferies raises Titagarh Rail target price by 23%. Check upside potential and key triggers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferies raised its target for Titagarh Rail Systems, citing strong execution and a robust order book. articles.title: Ronaldo, Taylor Swift and Mickey Mouse are fighting for your attention
articles.rephrased_article: A study by IPAM, Portugal's marketing institute, found that hosting the 2026 World Cup would generate an estimated 945 million euros in economic impact, even if Portugal does not advance beyond the group stage. articles.title: ₹7,597-crore NH upgradation project approved for Telangana, to boost regional connectivity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central government approved a ₹7,597 crore national highway upgradation project for four-laning of 190.76 km stretch of the National Highway (NH)-63 and NH-563 in north Telangana. The project will widen the Armoor-Jagtial-Mancherial section of NH-63 to four-lane standards on HAM, and the Jagtial-Karimnagar section of NH-563 under BOT (Toll) Mode. articles.title: Rajesh Exports: Sebi finds 97-99% revenue inflation, bars promoter from trading - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the market regulator, has issued an interim order against Rajesh Exports, a gold refiner and jewellery manufacturer, alleging that approximately 97-99% of its revenue may be inflated. articles.title: Market correction nearing its end; bet on banking, pharma: Rohit Srivastava - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Srivastava, a market expert, believes the Nifty is approaching a key technical support zone that could signal an end to the current correction. The energy sector and metals are also seen as potential areas for investment due to improving commodity trends. articles.title: IndusInd Bank shares fall 3% after fresh whistleblower complaint reaches PMO, RBI - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A whistleblower has filed a complaint alleging insider trading and financial irregularities at IndusInd Bank, including manipulation of financial records, evergreening of microfinance loans, suppression of audit findings, and attempts to conceal irregularities. The complaint also alleges that former zonal head of eastern India, Samir Agarwal, generated significant profits through share transactions using confidential information. articles.title: ITC shares fall 3% to fresh 52-week low; Motilal Oswal sees more pain ahead - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ITC shares dropped to a 52-week low on Wednesday, following the decline of IT stocks. articles.title: As El Niño threatens monsoon, farmer groups promote millets, mulching and drip irrigation | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Agriculture is working to support farmers facing challenges from a weak southwest monsoon by promoting drought-resistant crops and climate-resilient farming practices. The ministry has identified farmer-producer organizations (FPOs) across the country that are cultivating drought-resistant crops like millets, and is holding webinars to educate farmers on these methods.  The Ministry plans to use the network of over 63 lakh farmers from 10,000 FPOs to encourage adoption of climate-resilient practices, including alternative crops and moisture conservation techniques.

articles.title: Indians run some of the world's biggest companies. Why do we build so few of them?
articles.rephrased_article: Indian leaders are increasingly prominent in global corporations, but the article argues that this success stems from a highly competitive environment rather than inherent intelligence or cultural factors.  The pressure to succeed within India's social and economic system fosters resilience and discipline, qualities valued by large organizations. This high-pressure talent filter produces individuals who excel at managing complexity and enduring uncertainty, characteristics often overlooked in discussions about leadership. However, the article cautions that this relentless pressure can also lead to burnout and discourage creativity. The focus should shift from simply supplying CEOs to creating a system that fosters both resilience and innovation.

articles.title: Eternal to ICICI Bank: 15 stocks on Axis Securities buy list for June - Add to cart | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Axis Securities has recommended 15 stocks across various market segments for June, expecting upside potential of up to 44% in its top picks. Experts advise against relying on a single product like fixed deposits or mutual funds, recommending instead a diversified portfolio combining instruments such as annuities, SWPs, Balanced Advantage Funds, and growth assets. articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government is proposing a centralized portal to facilitate the migration of LPG consumers to PNG. articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty IT index surged 4.2% on Tuesday, reaching its highest point since May 2025, driven by improving global software sentiment and growing enterprise AI adoption. The discussion highlighted the complex pricing practices of hospitals and insurance companies, which often negotiate reimbursement rates that are significantly higher than independent imaging centers' prices. articles.rephrased_article: Iran's annual inflation rate surged to 77.2% in May, marking the highest level since World War II and reflecting a deepening economic crisis. articles.rephrased_article: IndiGo will cease flights to Manchester from August 31, citing escalating operational costs and airspace constraints.
